# REQ-002 source audit

Base: \`0ae1a69261c3fca12bad8bb62021f5fce8d6db2c\`. Its [reassessment](../../req-029/tmp/req-029-reassessment.md) proposes one explicitly shared object, read-first delivery and a separate comment grant. These are candidate scope choices. The roadmap IDs establish historical intent, and the [documentation guidelines](../docs/DOCUMENTATION_GUIDELINES.md) govern current ownership.

## Original scope

- **T041 — define the contract.** No-install browser viewing and commenting, configurable link or link plus code. Choose formats, separate permissions, commenter identity and granularity, revisions, expiry, revocation and host-offline behavior. Editing is deferred.
- **T042 — scoped viewing and link controls.** Reuse the appropriate host and identity owners. View only the published scope. Validate code changes, revocation, hostile paths/assets and interrupted sessions.
- **T043 — comments and revision-aware review.** Implement the chosen placement, identity, persistence and updates. Validate revision changes, duplicate submissions and permission revocation under bounded resource use.

## Boundaries at the base

- The local agent listener is exact-host loopback and rejects browser Origin and Fetch Metadata. Its grants cover local agent operations. A review host needs a distinct browser authorization boundary. The committed Pages workflow publishes the public site and help. The sibling PWA prototype concerns a separate mobile client and gateway. [Agent HTTP contract](../docs/bot-integrations.md#local-agent-http-access) · [Pages workflow](../.github/workflows/pages.yml) · [REQ-029 baseline](../../req-029/tmp/req-029-product-baseline.md#6-web-and-pwa)
- Group access is account-grant based, and ordinary file transfer has exact-offer consent and completion boundaries. A review grant should authorize only the explicitly published scope. Membership, device enrollment, account keys, history and arbitrary files remain outside that authority. Protected content has explicit copy, forward and save restrictions that publication must preserve. [Network design](../docs/network-design-reference.md) · [Protected messages](../docs/privacy-controls.md#protected-messages)
- Existing post offices provide bounded encrypted custody over reachable trusted routes. Browser reachability and review availability need their own contract. [Topology matrix](../docs/network-topologies.md#scenario-matrix)

## Decisions still open

1. **Publication.** Choose the initial content type and publisher authority, snapshot versus live revision, and the permitted preview, download and embedded asset scope.
2. **Hosting.** Choose the operator and reachable topology, supported browsers, trusted HTTPS origin and host/key authority. Specify lock, sleep, restart and host-offline behavior.
3. **Grants.** Define link-only versus link-plus-code defaults, forwarding semantics, code rotation, expiry and revocation for in-flight sessions. Specify what persists locally in a recipient browser and what can still be retrieved after revocation.
4. **Comments.** Decide whether comments ship after scoped viewing, who can comment, how authorship is represented, what revision or location anchors each comment, and who owns persistence, moderation, retention and duplicate handling.

Evidence is limited to local Git records, committed documents and sibling notes. Browser and host behavior were not exercised.
EOF
